title: Permutation in String
summary: Return whether any contiguous substring of s2 uses exactly the same letters and multiplicities as s1.

contractDetails.constraints: Both strings have 1–10,000 lowercase English letters.

statement: Return whether any contiguous substring of s2 uses exactly the same letters and multiplicities as s1. The matching substring may arrange the letters in any order.

examples.explanation: The middle three letters have two a's and one b.
The needed letters never appear together in a length-three window.
The entire second string is a valid rearrangement.

constraints: Both strings have 1–10,000 lowercase English letters.
hints: Conceptual: Every candidate substring has the same length as s1.
Directional: Compare letter counts in a window of that fixed size.
Implementation: When the window shifts, remove the departing letter and add the incoming one. Return true at the first exact count match.
complexityAnalysis: O(26(|s1| + |s2|)) time and O(26) auxiliary space with fixed-size count arrays. Sliding updates avoid recounting entire substrings.
